why: Real live incident (Dallas Cowboys Community, 2026-09-29 03:11 run): 8 of 19 candidate attempts were distinct, real, current stories (Joey Porter Jr. contract talk, P.J. Locke's IR move, a Jerry Jones/Micah Parsons-brother feud, a rival Packers trade, a Jake Ferguson fine) all rejected TOPIC_FREQUENCY_ENTITY_CAP or DOMINANT_NARRATIVE_CAP because every one resolved primaryEntity='cowboys' -- most of these headlines open with 'Cowboys ...' before the specific name, and matchedEntityNames' ordering (checks.ts) picks whichever match occurs first in the text. Same mechanism also picks the photo-search subject, so a specific-player story renders with a generic team photo instead of the actual player. Sets is_team_identity=true (see EntitySlot's own comment, types.ts) on every bare team/org-identity slot added or widened by the 2026-09-25/26 keyword patches, on the pages that showed the same shape in their own live rejection logs. Also splits Jerry Jones and Joe Gibbs -- real, recurring individual newsmakers, not the team itself -- out of the team slot's keyword list into their own dedicated slot, matching how every other named person is already registered; otherwise they'd inherit the team-level deprioritization too.
